newsitem.title: USA: Fund manager bets on Nu Horizons - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Fund manager bets on Nu Horizons - Barron's.

text.p: Delphi Management President Scott Black, who runs about $700 million in pension funds, looks to buy shares of small technology companies selling near their lows, Barron's said.
Among his recent finds is Nu Horizons Electronics Corp whose shares have fallen because of lower earnings, the investor weekly newspaper said in its May 26 edition.
The company distributes electronic components and Black believes the electronics business and its recently-soft prices should improve soon, Barron's said.
He also liked Zilog Inc, a California-based company which makes chips for consumer electronics, the paper said.
He said the company had a leading market position and good facilities, and its customers included AT&T Corp, Seagate Technology Inc and Hewlett-Packard Co, Barron's reported.
Black also remained positive on shares of Cohu Inc, which he believed could earn close to $3 per share in 1998, the newspaper said.
Barron's is a publication of Dow Jones & Co Inc.
